description: A digital to analogue converter: it reads up to eight logic inputs as a binary number and puts out a matching voltage.

params.text: How many of the eight bit inputs are read, from 2 to 8. Inputs above the setting are ignored, and the output range is spread across the ones that remain.
The output voltage produced when every bit in use is high, from 0V to 10V.
Adds between -5V and +5V to the converted voltage.

inputs.text: The least significant bit of the number being converted, worth one step.
The second bit of the number, worth two steps.
The third bit of the number, worth four steps. It is ignored while BITS is set to 2.
The fourth bit of the number, worth eight steps. It is ignored while BITS is set below 4.
The fifth bit of the number, worth sixteen steps. It is ignored while BITS is set below 5.
The sixth bit of the number, worth thirty-two steps. It is ignored while BITS is set below 6.
The seventh bit of the number, worth sixty-four steps. It is ignored while BITS is set below 7.
The most significant bit of the number, worth one hundred and twenty-eight steps. It is ignored unless BITS is set to 8.

outputs.text: The converted voltage: the scale voltage divided into equal steps across the bits in use, plus the offset, clipped to the range 0V to 12V.

notes: A logic input counts as high once it rises above 2V and does not count as low again until it falls below 0.1V; a logic output is 10V for high and 0V for low.
With the SCALE knob at 0V the converter stops writing to the output jack, which holds whatever voltage it last carried rather than falling to 0V. Turn SCALE up again to get it moving.
